findings.title: Preserve received launch receipts before tearing down the attachment
findings.impact: A successfully launched agent can be left running while recovery attaches to the previous agent, or reports an ended empty attachment for CLI start. This violates the acknowledged-launch continuity contract without requiring the launch reply itself to be lost.
findings.evidence: NativeControl's worker sends the successful Op::Launch result through rx; only poll/received transfers that target into launched (src/tui/control.rs:284-300, 627-635). While that reply arrives, the UI can already be blocked in acp-inspect or snapshot on the independent observation socket (src/tui.rs:1124-1139, 1192-1193). If that observation fails, execution reaches authority.stop at line1889 without another poll; stop clears launched and the receiver is subsequently dropped. Resume therefore still names the previous target. There is also a direct variant at lines1062-1067: poll can receive the successful launch and then a transport failure, but connected() is checked before take_launched(), so the known receipt is discarded there too. The existing LaunchObservation regression cuts the receipt-following snapshot, not an already-in-flight observation whose failure races the successful receipt.
findings.fix: Fence and join the old worker without replaying queued work, then retain any already received successful launch result solely as recovery continuity before dropping its reply channel. Update Resume from that exact acknowledged target even when either socket has failed, and consume known launch continuity before the connected() early return. Add fault coverage for an observation already in flight when the launch acknowledgement arrives, plus launch success followed by authority failure before UI consumption.

findings.title: Reclaim idle registrations created by failed automatic recovery attempts
findings.impact: Repeated recovery failures consume the daemon's finite controller registry until new native attachments and controller registrations fail with controller-busy. The abandoned recovery controllers' private handles are lost, preventing normal caller cleanup.
findings.evidence: attached registers a new NativeControl at line917 before connecting the observation socket, obtaining its snapshot or validating continuity (lines921-924). supervise retries connection failures automatically after recovery_wait. Every failed attempt drops/stops NativeControl, but stop only shuts down its stream and joins the worker (src/tui/control.rs:361-374). Daemon connection departure calls Registry::depart; depart_at only sets view.connected=false and retains the controller (src/control.rs:855-869). Controller registration rejects once self.controllers.len() reaches4096 (src/control.rs:447-449), and removal requires explicit close_controller. Thus even attempts that never established an observation or acquired any authority permanently spend registrations; automatic retry introduces an unbounded producer against that retained limit.
findings.fix: Avoid spending a controller registration before a fresh observation and continuity check where possible, and provide bounded cleanup for disconnected recovery registrations proven to have no ownership or pending claims. Preserve original owners, retained claims/work and fresh-connection provenance; do not release authority or cancel claims merely to reclaim registrations. Add a source-derived recovery fault regression that confirms repeated failed observer setup does not monotonically consume controller admission capacity.

report.summary: FAIL: 14 of 16 applicable control areas passed source review (87.5%). One must-fix launch-receipt recovery race and one should-fix automatic-recovery registration leak remain; both are introduced by the new native launch/recovery lifecycle and traced through their consuming paths.
report.limits: Independent, read-only source review of the frozen E06 manifest, base2195b05 patch and relevant existing consumers. No files edited; no builds, tests, lint, formatting, runtime/CLI/version probes, browser or provider calls executed. No prior review reports, dispositions or self-audits read. No credential/auth databases, prohibited private runtime directory, raw provider/session/wire output or unrelated worktrees inspected. Findings are source-proven causal paths, not runtime reproductions. Parent runtime receipts were not substituted for code reasoning; complete installed-OMP live acceptance and remaining authorization were not exercised or independently certified.
